summary.text: Jasmine Clark is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 13th District, an open seat. A microbiologist who teaches at Emory University's nursing school, she has represented Georgia House District 108 since 2019 after defeating a Republican incumbent in 2018. She is running for Congress on a platform her campaign describes as defending healthcare, science-based policy, and democratic institutions.

paragraphs.text: Born in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1982; Wikipedia lists a Bachelor of Science from the University of Tennessee.
Earned a Ph.D. in microbiology from Emory University.

Works as a scientist and instructor at Emory University's Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing; directed the 2017 March for Science in Atlanta and has worked with the Georgia Alliance for Social Justice.
Won Georgia House District 108 on November 6, 2018, defeating incumbent Republican Clay Cox; took office January 14, 2019. Her campaign website says she flipped a long-held Republican seat.

Won re-election to the Georgia House in 2020, 2022, and 2024. Her committee assignments in the 2025-2026 session include Banks and Banking, Budget and Fiscal Affairs Oversight, Health, Higher Education, and Interstate Cooperation.
Announced her candidacy for Congress in June 2025, initially challenging incumbent Rep. David Scott in the Democratic primary, and won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.1% of the vote.
Lived in Lilburn, Georgia, as of 2020, according to Ballotpedia.
